theory.intro: Kilometres measure long distances. A kilometre is just $1000$ metres, so we can change between the two units by multiplying or dividing by $1000$.
facts: To change **metres to kilometres**, divide by $1000$.
To change **kilometres to metres**, multiply by $1000$.
steps: Decide which unit is larger (km) and which is smaller (m).
Multiply by $1000$ to go km $\to$ m; divide by $1000$ to go m $\to$ km.
Write the answer with the correct unit.

foundation.question_text: How many metres are in $1$ kilometre?

A fun run is $2$ kilometres long.
Record its distance using the abbreviation for kilometres.

development.question_text: Write $1$ kilometre $300$ metres using the abbreviations km and m.
Write $2400$ metres as kilometres and metres.
Write $6\text{ km }50\text{ m}$ entirely in metres.
Which is farther: $4\text{ km}$ or $3900\text{ m}$?
development.solution_text:
$4\text{ km}=4000\text{ m}$
$4000\text{ m}>3900\text{ m}$
$4\text{ km}$ is farther.

development.question_text:
A walking track is $1\text{ km }750\text{ m}$ long.
Record the whole distance in metres.

A sign says the lookout is $3200$ metres away.
Record this as kilometres and metres.

mastery.question_text:
A trail has two sections: $2\text{ km}$ and $650\text{ m}$.
Record the total length in metres.
Order these distances from shortest to longest: $1800\text{ m}$, $2\text{ km}$, $1\text{ km }950\text{ m}$.
mastery.solution_text:
$2\text{ km}=2000\text{ m}$
$1\text{ km }950\text{ m}=1950\text{ m}$
$1800\text{ m},\ 1\text{ km }950\text{ m},\ 2\text{ km}$

mastery.question_text:
A route is $5\text{ km}$ long.
After $3750\text{ m}$, how many metres remain?
